title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Waterfront, Vancouver, BC, Canada


The first few weeks of the Master of Data Science (MDS) program have been an incredible experience. As a newcomer to Vancouver, this program is giving me the perfect opportunity to explore and settle into this beautiful city. Just recently, I took a walk along the downtown waterfront, and it was stunning. There is nothing quite like a peaceful stroll right along the edge of the Pacific Ocean to clear your mind.
Back on campus, the MDS orientation set a great tone for the months ahead. It was structured so thoughtfully that all the new information felt manageable rather than overwhelming. The best part? Meeting my classmates. Everyone comes from such diverse backgrounds, and I am genuinely excited to learn alongside them throughout the program.
One thing that surprised me is just how established the MDS program is. Knowing that there is a large, active network of alumni working across so many different industries gives me a huge confidence boost. I am really looking forward to connecting with them and learning from their real-world experiences.
Here’s to the next chapter!

I bridge the gap between complex engineering systems and data-driven solutions. With a background in Biomedical Engineering, I transitioned into Data Science and have spent the last decade leading high-impact projects across biomedical, energy, finance, and real estate industries.
Throughout my career, I’ve tackled diverse challenges, from building human brain models and automating drilling operations to engineering enterprise-scale data quality systems, performing root cause analysis, and training AI models.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
I’ve always been driven by the power of Data Science, but seeing it in action across industry transformed that passion into a purpose. A single well-crafted algorithm has the power to drive massive, real-world impact. In oil and gas, it means optimizing drilling parameters to save millions of dollars and prevent costly operational failures. In banking, it means building automated data quality systems that protect millions from financial loss while elevating the customer experience. For me, data science isn’t just about code—it’s about engineering solutions that reshape how entire industries operate.
